lines.text: Tuesday, an agent loses an hour. The app will not start, because another stack is squatting on port three thousand.
Finally it works out the fix. Use port three thousand three hundred, and the whole thing runs.
But the chat ends, and so does the lesson. Tomorrow another agent will have to find it all out again.
Agent R Q has workspace memory. Before it finishes, the agent saves that one line, and moves on.
Memory is a small index with links to short entries. Every gotcha gets its own page, so nothing gets buried.
On the next task, any agent reads the index first. That is the rule, and agents follow it before they touch code.
Wednesday, a different agent in a different tool reads it, and goes straight to port three thousand three hundred.
It works for Claude, Codex and Gemini alike, on any machine, because the memory lives in the workspace, not on a laptop.
And you can read and edit it yourself. If a gotcha goes stale, fix the entry or delete it, like any other note.
Over a few weeks, the list grows. Every trap you hit once becomes a signpost for every agent after.
Keep each gotcha to a line or two. Short entries get read, long ones get skipped.
Hit a trap once, and never again. Try workspace memory at Agent R Q dot com.
